findings.summary: Feature review 3 of 5 at dd5ddff: pass. Since dcf0346 only the attributed r2 record was added, and the CUA source_blobs match the dcf0346 runtime exactly. The controller's dd5ddff checks pass 221/221 tests, plus the build, the protected 04-C checks and all three probes. This round closes R2's reading-coverage gap. In this session I read every mandated original through EOF in bounded chunks. App files: review-service 1–477, review-journal 1–131, review-page 1–268, consent-service 1–92, child-setup 1–100, generation-journal 1–17, continuation-journal 1–123, request-queue 1–199. Planning: ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1 1–411, MODULE_GUIDE 1–27, and the complete JSON bodies of setup-r1 through setup-r5. Also read in full in this session: generation-service, queue-journal, founder-auth, loop-auth, migrations 001, 003, 007, 008, 012, 013 and 014, 00-B CONTRACTS 1–318, 00-C SCREEN_CONTRACT_MAP 1–174, COST_LEDGER, COST_VIEWS, the 05-D card, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, the three approved execution copies, the engineering README and REVIEW_NOTES, the spec, the full diff of all ten paths plus the R2 hunks, and the root probe. I checked the direct SQL in cost against the modules that own those tables. Consent: cost reads the latest service_consents row by epoch, requiring state 'active' and policy TEST-v1; consent-service writes those rows the same way, with withdraw/re-record each creating a new epoch row. Profile: cost reads child_setup_profiles.current_version and consent_epoch; child-setup increments the version under a deferred version-matching trigger, so the cost FK to child_profile_versions is valid. Queue: project() only reads, under FOR UPDATE, returns accepted scope/state, and fails denied or journal_unavailable. Founder sessions: revoked_at and expires_at are checked with the same boundary as requireFounder. Lock order: cost takes household → consent → founder → request → profile → generation rows, which matches the generation and review authorities and the design's household/consent-first order. Cost calls queue.founderRead and generation.read outside serializeQueueWork, which avoids the deadlock, since both use that serializer internally. Generation's read only writes through the expired-running-lease path; cost never reads running jobs. Migration 013 makes the attempt fence immutable; CancelJob raises the job fence by one and marks the attempt cancelled; queued-then-cancelled gives fence 1 / version 2. The cost inventory checks match all three. Cost improves on review in two places: payload binding uses the recorded actor and epoch rather than the current session, and the journal marker binds its own file identity, the directory and the log, while review's marker binds only the namespace. All prior findings are rechecked. R1's majors and minors are fixed, as R2 confirmed. R2's coverage minor is resolved by this round. R2's held-append nit is resolved by a fresh native held-append observation at dd5ddff. The reconsent-gate nit stays as a disclosed limitation. These remain open and are not closed by this review: all real-world gates; full 05-A/05-B/05-D/05-G/11-C; the setup-r4 loop-wide review-ceiling minor; the reconsent profile limitation and the 64-marker limit; the missing uncaptured attempt-to-job map; and the fact that literal browser zoom was not observed natively.

findings.title: Remaining reading limits outside the mandated set (precise disclosure)
findings.problem: Every original that this round and R1 named as mandatory is now read through EOF in this session. Not read through EOF, and not listed as mandated: PROJECT_CONTEXT (only lines 10-21, 225-236 and the changelog lines found by grep), AGENTS.md, GOVERNANCE.md, PRODUCT_V1, the 11-A/11-B task cards (their COST_LEDGER/COST_VIEWS outputs were read in full), migrations 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010 and 011 (009 only via grep for wonder_requests), the generation test file beyond its fixture helpers (lines 1-75), the queue-client, review-client, wonder-capture and production modules, and the earlier generation/review slice REPORTs. Cost touches none of these directly beyond the tables already checked against their owners.
findings.fix_check: No action unless the controller expands the mandated reading set.

findings.title: Reconsent denial still uses the existing profile-epoch gate (carried)
findings.problem: child-setup.mjs keeps child_setup_profiles.consent_epoch at its creation epoch, so after withdrawal and reconsent the profile is 'blocked'. Cost, like generation and review, denies on profile.consent_epoch !== epoch. The reconsent test therefore proves denial through this known same-household reconsent limitation, not through a check specific to cost.
findings.fix_check: Keep the reconsent profile limitation disclosed in the REPORT and acceptance receipt.

findings.title: 05-D criterion 3 per-attempt lineage is outside this partial slice
findings.problem: The CODEX-05-D card asks every billable attempt to record its model, prompt, pattern and usage cost (estimate versus actual). The frozen Attempt shape records IDs, state, fence, lease and revision IDs, with unknown usage and cash, but not provider/model/prompt/pattern versions; those stay on generation revisions. This matches the setup-passed spec, and full 05-D stays OPEN, but the acceptance receipt should state the gap.
findings.fix_check: The partial acceptance receipt lists per-attempt lineage capture as remaining full-05-D work.

findings.title: dd5ddff held-append screenshot does not show the status line
findings.problem: dd5ddff-cua-held-confirmed.png shows the form and the fictional comparison pool, but not the 'Original operation in progress' or 'Saved:' status text. The evidence that Saved clears during a held append rests on the textual CUA observation and the passing HTTP-to-DOM held-transport regression. Together these are adequate, but the screenshot alone does not show the status transition.
findings.fix_check: Optionally, a future native record captures the status region during the held and released states.

findings.title: Review-journal marker lacks the identity binding cost now has (pre-existing)
findings.problem: Informational, outside cost scope. The review marker authenticates only format and namespace (lines 52-81). It does not bind directory, log or marker file identity, so the same byte-identical marker copy that drove cost-journal-v2 could be adopted after a review restart. Cost does not depend on it, and protected review sources must stay unchanged in this slice.
findings.fix_check: Record as a carried observation for a separately scoped review-slice follow-up. No change in COST-LOCAL-01.
